ledger.why: the reward is text only: 'learning' is not a skill

items.text: being left behind when the older children go exploring
forgetting the faces of people from (child.his/her) old home
being laughed at for making mistakes
growing up and leaving the nursery
failing at a skill that everyone else seems to understand
being told that crying is childish
The adult recalls a time when (adult.he/she) was frightened and somebody helped. The child asks what happened next.
The adult admits that (adult.he/she) still gets scared sometimes. The child looks surprised.
The adult tells a ridiculous story about mistaking a harmless crab for a terrible monster. The child giggles.
The adult talks too much. The child finally interrupts: "I didn't want a story. I wanted you to stay."
The child asks for company, not advice. They sit together.
The child wants to try the frightening activity with help.
The child says (child.he/she) doesn't know. The adult says that not knowing is an acceptable answer.
The child asks whether the adult will be angry if (child.he/she) cries. The adult says no.
The child joins the other children for a short while, then returns when (child.he/she) has had enough.
The child stays beside the adult until sunset. No grand breakthrough occurs, but (child.he/she) feels safer.
The child makes a new friend who is afraid of the same thing.
The child says, "Maybe I can be brave tomorrow." The adult replies, "You don't have to do everything tomorrow."
The child takes the adult's hand, then lets go when ready.

question.name: Afraid
question.text:
A young villager, (Child), has been avoiding the other children. When a caregiver, (Adult), asks what is wrong, (Child) admits that (child.he/she) is afraid of {A}.
(Adult) {sits beside the child|keeps a respectful distance|offers a cup of water|waits quietly for (child.him/her) to continue}.

choices.label: TELL A STORY ABOUT BEING AFRAID.
ASK WHAT THE CHILD NEEDS RIGHT NOW.
